summary: Tested customer profile photo (AvatarUpload) feature end-to-end: backend validation (profile avatar_url prefix guard, /api/upload image guard, HEIC acceptance) and frontend flows (upload, persist across reload, remove, sidebar sync, admin customer list avatar). All backend tests pass (7/7). All frontend flows pass. Regression checks (banner-upload, Save Profile button, KYC form) look good. Test customer is left with an uploaded avatar as requested.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py upload_image: admins bypass the image mime check entirely (if role==admin). Admins can upload arbitrary files (any content_type). Low risk but worth gating by extension or MIME allowlist.

AvatarUpload.remove() doesn't call setUser directly from response; it relies on save('') which does setUser(data). OK, but if save fails toast is 'Could not remove photo' with no error detail; consider formatApiErrorDetail for parity with pick().

ProfileIn.avatar_url validator is in _apply_profile_update, not in Pydantic schema. Admin profile-update endpoints (if any) that use ProfileIn and bypass _apply_profile_update would skip this check. Confirmed /api/profile uses _apply_profile_update, so OK, but keep in mind for future admin edit endpoints.
